sources.title_iast: Viṣṇusahasranāma recitation preface (Sanjeev Abhyankar performance sequence)

sources.title_iast: Thousand Ways to the Transcendental: reviewed embedded-Gītā word analysis
sources.witness: Reviewed analysis for all 142 identified Gītā fragments in Chinmayananda's commentary. Printed wording and loci are preserved against the authorized scan, the Sanskrit is reconciled with the local BORI witness, 215 unresolved morpheme glosses were repaired, and all 193 root occurrences were checked against the shared Prakriya Sanskrit-source library's Dhātupāṭha; the interpreter was not used.
sources.notes: The public block order is Devanāgarī, interactive IAST, then English with bidirectional Sanskrit-English hover and click. All 85 English translations supplied by Chinmayananda preserve his wording exactly; the 57 Gītā blocks he leaves without English receive separately provenance-marked site literal translations. The packet covers 1,222 word instances and records direct source-library review; site English is never attributed to Chinmayananda.

sources.title_iast: Thousand Ways to the Transcendental: Viṣṇu Sahasranāma commentary
sources.witness: Swami Chinmayananda, Thousand Ways to the Transcendental: Vishnu Sahasranaama, Central Chinmaya Mission Trust, ISBN 978-81-7597-245-2; structured transcription checked against the owner's 272-page scan, with canonical IAST and Devanagari name headings and reviewed normalization of Sanskrit romanization.
sources.notes: The owner explicitly authorized proceeding on the basis of permission from Chinmaya Mission. Chinmayananda's scan-backed opening and full commentary remain attributed source prose in Full mode. The separate simple_meaning field is a site-generated or site-selected concise reading derived from that commentary and is explicitly not credited as Chinmayananda's translation or quotation; replayable source excerpts are retained separately as review evidence. Scan-checked preface engagement is stored separately in gita/vishnu-sahasranama/preface-commentary.json. The improved TXT OCR (SHA-256 8e87779ac1ac0555c9b12b62e895c2338bc8e6c5cf2e0cc82b9f9d69557f36a4) is comparison-only: it exposed useful readings but also truncated names 742 and 817, so no reading is promoted without page-image or independent-witness confirmation.
